CAPACITY PLAN: KAFKA MESSAGE QUEUE AT 4,200 MSG/S PEAK WITH 3X BURST ALLOWANCE (12,600 MSG/S) - ITERATION 1

All figures below are canonical. The consistency matrix in Step 4 audits that each shared figure carries the same value in every section where it appears.

STEP 0 - ASSUMPTIONS REGISTER (decisions made in lieu of a spec; each is overridable, see Step 6)
A1 Technology: Apache Kafka 3.7+ in KRaft mode (no ZooKeeper), self-hosted on AWS EC2 in us-east-1, one broker per AZ across 3 AZs. Rationale: the requested cost model is per broker, which requires a self-hosted, broker-scaled system; Kafka partition/replication arithmetic is deterministic per broker; 12,600 msg/s is comfortably within a 3-node cluster. Rejected alternatives: Amazon SQS (managed, no broker unit to price), RabbitMQ quorum queues (workable at this rate but coarser scale-out and less predictable per-broker throughput under 2:1 fan-out reads).
A2 Message sizes: average 1 KiB (1,024 bytes); maximum 1 MiB (Kafka default max record size).
A3 Peak sustained ingress: 4,200 msg/s (the normal, non-burst design rate).
A4 Burst allowance: 3 x peak = 12,600 msg/s, sustained up to 60 seconds, at most 4 bursts per rolling hour (worst-case burst duty cycle 240 s/hour, about 6.7%).
A5 Read:write ratio 2:1 - two consumer groups, each reading 100% of the stream.
A6 Retention: 72 hours, time-based, single main topic, no compaction.
A7 Durability: replication factor 3, min.insync.replicas=2, producer acks=all with idempotence.
A8 Availability: 99.9% target; the cluster tolerates one broker failure with writes continuing (ISR=2 meets min ISR); MTTR objective 4 hours.
A9 Scope: single region, 3 AZs; no multi-region DR.
A10 Clients: about 50 producers; 24 consumers (2 groups x 12). Producer config: linger.ms=5, batch.size=64 KiB, lz4 compression, acks=all.
A11 Pricing: USD, AWS us-east-1 on-demand list prices, 730 h/month convention for compute, costed at the peak sustained rate held 24x7 (conservative upper bound). Verify current prices before purchase; reserved capacity cuts compute 30-60%.
A12 Consumers are in-region, so public internet egress is $0.

STEP 1 - SIZING SECTION

1.1 Workload model (canonical rates used by every other section):
- Ingress, messages/s: peak 4,200 | burst 12,600
- Ingress, bytes/s at 1 KiB avg: peak 4.10 MiB/s (4,200 x 1,024 = 4,300,800 B/s; 4,300,800 / 1,048,576 = 4.10) | burst 12.30 MiB/s (12,600 x 1,024 = 12,902,400 B/s; 12,902,400 / 1,048,576 = 12.30)
- Consumer reads (2:1): peak 8,400 msg/s = 8.20 MiB/s | burst 25,200 msg/s = 24.61 MiB/s

1.2 Topology: 3 brokers (combined broker+controller, KRaft), one per AZ; one main topic with 24 partitions (8 leader partitions per broker, even distribution); RF=3; min.insync.replicas=2; acks=all.

1.3 Per-broker load (per-broker written bytes = RF x cluster ingress / 3 brokers = cluster ingress):
- Leader produce: 1,400 msg/s (1.37 MiB/s) peak | 4,200 msg/s (4.10 MiB/s) burst
- Follower replication in: 2,800 msg/s (2.73 MiB/s) peak | 8,400 msg/s (8.20 MiB/s) burst
- Replication out (serving other brokers' followers): 2.73 MiB/s peak | 8.20 MiB/s burst
- Consumer reads served: 2,800 msg/s (2.73 MiB/s) peak | 8,400 msg/s (8.20 MiB/s) burst
- Disk write per broker: 4.10 MiB/s peak | 12.30 MiB/s burst. Derivation: leader writes 1.37 MiB/s + follower writes 2.73 MiB/s = 4.10 MiB/s at peak; x3 at burst = 12.30 MiB/s. Equivalently 4,200 msg/s x 1 KiB = 4.10 MiB/s and 12,600 msg/s x 1 KiB = 12.30 MiB/s written per broker.
- NIC per broker (in+out): 9.57 MiB/s (~80 Mbit/s) peak | 28.71 MiB/s (~241 Mbit/s) burst, under 2.5% of the m5 family 10 Gbps. Derivation: in = 1.37 produce + 2.73 replication in = 4.10; out = 2.73 replication out + 2.73 consumer reads = 5.47; total 9.57 MiB/s; x3 at burst = 28.71 MiB/s.
- CPU design targets: 40% of 8 vCPU at peak | 70% at burst

1.4 Storage sizing:
- Retained data per broker = 72 h x peak ingress = 4,300,800 B/s x 259,200 s = 1.115 x 10^12 B = 1,115 GB (~1.01 TiB); equivalently 371.6 GB/day or 15.5 GB/hour.
- Burst delta: one 60 s burst adds 12,600 x 60 x 1 KiB = 774 MB (738 MiB) per broker = 0.04% of the volume (negligible).
- Provision: 2,000 GB gp3 per broker, steady utilization 56% (1,115/2,000). gp3 baseline 3,000 IOPS / 125 MB/s is roughly 10x the 12.30 MiB/s (12.9 MB/s) burst write rate.

1.5 Compute sizing: one m5.2xlarge (8 vCPU, 32 GiB) per broker. JVM heap 6 GiB (G1GC), leaving about 24 GiB page cache = about 100 minutes of hot log at the peak write rate (24 GiB / 4.10 MiB/s = ~5,994 s), 20x the 300 s maximum tolerated consumer lag. Estimated request load at burst: 4,000-5,000 requests/s per broker (produce + fetch + replication), well within an 8-vCPU broker. Security baseline (TLS 1.2+ in transit, SASL/SCRAM or mTLS auth) is carried inside these CPU targets; encryption at these line rates adds roughly 10-15% CPU, already covered by the 40%/70% design targets.

1.6 Consumer-side sizing (justifies the lag thresholds in 3.2): each consumer group sustains 6,300 msg/s (1.5x peak). During a 60 s burst the backlog grows at 12,600 - 6,300 = 6,300 msg/s, reaching 378,000 messages; expressed as lag-seconds (backlog / current ingress rate of 4,200) that is 90 s. After the burst it drains at a net 6,300 - 4,200 = 2,100 msg/s, clearing in 180 s (240 s total from burst start). With 12 consumers per group, per-consumer load is 350 msg/s steady and 525 msg/s during drain; 24 partitions allow scaling a group to 24 consumers.

1.7 N-1 degraded-burst check: one broker down during a 60 s burst leaves each surviving broker with 6,300 msg/s leader produce + 6,300 msg/s replication = 12.30 MiB/s disk write and 12.30 MiB/s consumer reads; CPU may transiently reach ~90% for under 60 s, below the 5-minute critical alert window in 3.2, and writes continue because ISR=2 still meets min.insync.replicas=2. Conclusion: 3 brokers, no spare; N+1 is covered by headroom.

STEP 2 - COST SECTION (priced per broker, USD, AWS us-east-1, on-demand list)

2.1 Per-broker monthly cost:
- Compute: m5.2xlarge (8 vCPU, 32 GiB) at $0.384/h x 730 h = $280.32
- Storage: 2,000 GB gp3 x $0.08/GB-month = $160.00
- Inter-AZ replication transfer: 5.47 MiB/s per broker (2.73 in + 2.73 out; with 3 brokers in 3 AZs all replication crosses AZ boundaries) x 2,592,000 s/month (30-day month) = 14,178,240 MiB = 14,867 GB x $0.01/GB = $148.67
- TOTAL PER BROKER: $588.99/month

2.2 Cluster totals: 3 x $588.99 = $1,766.97/month = $21,203.64/year. Sensitivity: at 50% average duty instead of 24x7 peak, inter-AZ drops to $74.34/broker, i.e. $514.66/broker and $1,543.98/month for the cluster.

2.3 Burst allowance impact on cost: $0 incremental. The 12,600 msg/s burst is absorbed by headroom already paid for in the per-broker price: CPU target 70% at burst vs 40% at peak; disk write 12.30 MiB/s vs the volume's 125 MB/s; NIC 241 Mbit/s vs 10 Gbps; storage delta 774 MB per burst (0.04% of the 2,000 GB volume). No additional brokers, IOPS, or bandwidth tiers are purchased for burst. This is how the 3x burst allowance is reflected in the cost section.

2.4 Exclusions: producer/consumer application infrastructure; monitoring stack (allow +$50-150/month cluster-wide if managed); public egress ($0 per A12; if consumers were external, $0.09/GB on 8.20 MiB/s (~22,285 GB/month) of reads would add about $2,000/month and force a re-plan); backups/DR (replication is the availability mechanism, per A9); software licenses (Kafka is open source, $0); labor and on-call.

STEP 3 - OPERATIONS SECTION (alert thresholds)

3.1 Metrics collected (15 s scrape, 1-minute aggregation, per broker and cluster): ingress messages/s and bytes/s; consumer-group lag in messages, with lag-seconds = backlog / current ingress rate; broker CPU %; disk used (GB and %); under-replicated partitions; offline partitions; per-partition ISR size; produce and fetch request p99 latency; NIC bytes in/out; broker liveness; KRaft controller quorum health.

3.2 Alert thresholds (Warning = ticket, next business hours; Critical = page on-call immediately):
1. Cluster ingress (msg/s): expected 4,200 peak / at most 12,600 for at most 60 s, at most 4/h. Warning: >8,400 sustained >120 s. Critical: >12,600 sustained >60 s.
2. Cluster ingress (bytes/s): expected 4.10 MiB/s / 12.30 MiB/s. Warning: >8.20 MiB/s >120 s. Critical: >12.30 MiB/s >60 s.
3. Consumer lag (lag-seconds): expected <60 s peak / at most 90 s (378,000-message backlog) during a sanctioned burst, cleared within 180 s. Warning: >60 s (>252,000 msgs) for 5 min. Critical: >300 s (>1,260,000 msgs) for 5 min.
4. Broker CPU (of 8 vCPU): expected 40% peak / 70% burst. Warning: >60% for 10 min. Critical: >75% for 5 min.
5. Disk used per broker (of 2,000 GB): expected ~56% (1,115 GB) / +774 MB per burst. Warning: >70% (1,400 GB) for 30 min. Critical: >80% (1,600 GB) or projected time-to-full <24 h.
6. Under-replicated partitions: expected 0 (transient during restart). Warning: >0 for 2 min. Critical: >0 for 10 min.
7. Offline partitions or any partition ISR <2: expected 0. Critical immediately on >0 (acks=all writes failing).
8. Produce request p99: expected <100 ms peak / <150 ms burst. Warning: >200 ms for 5 min. Critical: >1,000 ms for 5 min.
9. Fetch request p99: expected <200 ms peak / <300 ms burst. Warning: >500 ms for 5 min. Critical: >2,000 ms for 5 min.
10. Broker NIC: expected ~80 Mbit/s peak / ~241 Mbit/s burst. Warning: >5 Gbps for 5 min. Critical: >7 Gbps for 5 min.
11. Broker liveness: expected 3/3 up. Critical: any broker down >60 s (page; writes continue at ISR=2; 4 h MTTR).
12. KRaft controller quorum: expected healthy. Critical: no active controller >30 s.

Threshold rationale (each ties back to sizing):
- Alert 1: the 60 s critical window equals the sanctioned burst duration, so ingress above 12,600 msg/s for longer than 60 s is by definition unsanctioned overload; the warning (2x peak = 8,400 msg/s, 120 s window) never fires for a sanctioned 60 s burst.
- Alert 3: message equivalents derive from the 4,200 msg/s peak (60 s -> 252,000 msgs; 300 s -> 1,260,000 msgs); the 300 s critical bound is 3.3x the 90 s worst-case sanctioned-burst lag and tolerates a backlog 3.3x the 378,000-message sanctioned-burst backlog.
- Alert 4: both windows (10 min warning, 5 min critical) exceed the 60 s burst duration, so sanctioned bursts, including N-1 degraded bursts reaching ~90% CPU per 1.7, never page; sustained CPU above 60%/75% means the 4,200 msg/s peak assumption has been outgrown.
- Alert 5: the 56% steady baseline leaves 14 points of margin to the 70% warning; the time-to-full guard catches retention enforcement failure.

3.3 Burst-specific operations:
- Every event with ingress >8,400 msg/s is auto-annotated as a burst event (peak rate, duration, message count). Expected per event: at most 60 s, +774 MB disk per broker, CPU at most 70%, produce p99 <150 ms, consumer lag at most 90 s recovering within 180 s.
- Burst-budget warning: more than 4 burst events in a rolling hour -> Warning ticket; producer owners are exceeding the sanctioned burst model.
- Burst-duration critical: any burst >60 s is covered by alert 1 critical.

3.4 Runbook actions (abridged):
- Alert 1 critical: identify top producer client-ids; verify/enforce the per-producer Kafka quota of 300 msg/s (50 producers x 300 = 15,000 msg/s aggregate ceiling, above the 12,600 burst ceiling so sanctioned bursts are unaffected); escalate to the producer owner.
- Alert 3 critical: scale the lagging consumer group toward its 24-consumer ceiling (24 partitions = hard max); if lag persists with nominal broker metrics, the consumer application, not the queue, is the bottleneck.
- Alert 4 critical: check leader-partition balance (target 8 leaders per broker); rebalance via partition reassignment if skewed.
- Alert 5 critical: verify retention is enforced at 72 h; emergency lever: cut retention to 48 h (steady usage drops to ~743 GB/broker) while root-causing.
- Alerts 6/7/11 critical: replace the failed broker from its launch template, reassign its partitions, confirm ISR returns to 3 within 10 min of rejoin; MTTR objective 4 h.

3.5 Capacity-review triggers (re-run this plan when any fires): rolling 7-day mean ingress >2,100 msg/s (50% of the peak assumption); any warning from alerts 3, 4, or 8 firing more than 3x/week; burst events exceeding 4/hour or 60 s for 2 consecutive weeks; steady disk usage >70%.

STEP 4 - CROSS-SECTION CONSISTENCY MATRIX (audit table: every figure appearing in more than one section, with identical values)
- 4,200 msg/s peak: sizing 1.1/1.3/1.4/1.6 | cost 2.1 (inter-AZ basis) | ops 3.2 alerts 1-3
- 12,600 msg/s burst (3x peak): sizing 1.1/1.3/1.6/1.7 | cost 2.3 ($0 headroom) | ops 3.2 alert 1 critical, 3.3
- 60 s burst duration: sizing 1.6/1.7 | cost 2.3 | ops 3.2 alert 1 windows, 3.3
- 4 bursts/hour: sizing 1.6 duty assumption | cost 2.3 (no cost impact) | ops 3.3 burst-budget warning, 3.5
- 1 KiB average message: sizing 1.1/1.3/1.4 | cost 2.1 (storage and inter-AZ basis) | ops 3.2 alerts 1-2 byte equivalents
- 2,000 GB provisioned volume: sizing 1.4 | cost 2.1 ($160.00) | ops 3.2 alert 5
- 1,115 GB steady usage: sizing 1.4 | ops 3.2 alert 5 expected value
- 774 MB per burst: sizing 1.4 | cost 2.3 | ops 3.2 alert 5, 3.3
- m5.2xlarge 8 vCPU / 32 GiB: sizing 1.5 | cost 2.1 ($280.32) | ops 3.2 alert 4
- CPU 40% peak / 70% burst: sizing 1.3/1.5 | cost 2.3 | ops 3.2 alert 4, 3.5
- 72 h retention: sizing 1.4 | cost 2.1 (storage sizing) | ops 3.2 alert 5, 3.4
- 24 partitions: sizing 1.2/1.6 | ops 3.4 consumer ceiling
- RF=3, min ISR=2, acks=all: sizing 1.2/1.7 | cost 2.1 (inter-AZ volume) | ops 3.2 alerts 6, 7, 11
- 6,300 msg/s consumer capacity: sizing 1.6 | ops 3.2 alert 3 rationale
- 3 brokers: sizing 1.2/1.7 | cost 2.2 | ops 3.2 alert 11

STEP 5 - VALIDATION PROCEDURE (execute before accepting the plan as capacity truth)
1. Soak: 4,200 msg/s (1 KiB, 50 producers, acks=all) for 60 min with both consumer groups at full read. Pass: per-broker CPU 40% or less, produce p99 <100 ms, URP=0, lag <60 s, per-broker disk growth 15.5 GB/h +/-10%.
2. Burst: four 60 s bursts at 12,600 msg/s within one hour. Pass: CPU 70% or less, produce p99 <150 ms, consumer lag back below 60 s within 60 s of each burst end and to zero within 180 s, disk delta ~774 MB per burst, zero pages (burst annotations only).
3. Failover: kill one broker during burst 3. Pass: zero produce failures (ISR=2 meets min ISR), surviving brokers CPU <90% transient, broker-down critical fires within 60 s, no false criticals from alerts 4/8 (their 5-10 min windows exceed the 60 s burst).
4. Recovery: restart the broker; ISR returns to 3 and URP clears within 10 min.
5. Retention: 72 h at 4,200 msg/s; per-broker usage plateaus at ~1,115 GB (~56% of 2,000 GB).
6. Alert drill: inject a synthetic 13,000 msg/s for 90 s and a synthetic 400 s lag; verify alert 1 critical and alert 3 critical route to paging exactly per 3.2.

STEP 6 - RECOMPUTE INSTRUCTIONS (if any Step 0 assumption is overridden)
- Average message size S KiB: multiply every MiB/s figure, the 1,115 GB storage figure, and the $148.67 inter-AZ line by S; resize the volume to 1,115 x S GB plus headroom.
- Peak R msg/s: burst becomes 3R; lag equivalents become 60R and 300R messages; consumer capacity 1.5R; retained storage R x 1 KiB x 259,200 s per broker.
- Burst duration D s / frequency F per hour: alert 1 critical window becomes D; burst-budget warning becomes F; the 1.6 drain math recomputes as backlog (3R - 1.5R) x D draining at 0.5R msg/s net.
- Retention H hours: steady storage = 371.6 GB/day x H per broker; re-derive alert 5 thresholds against the provisioned volume.
- Broker count B / RF: per-broker stored bytes = RF x cluster ingress / B; per-broker cross-AZ rate = 2 x (RF-1) x ingress / B (all-AZ-spread assumption); recompute 2.1 inter-AZ and 1.3.
- Multi-region or external consumers: this plan is void; re-plan per A9/A12.
